summary.tldr: Creates a Criminal Code offence for publicly promoting hatred against Indigenous peoples by denying, downplaying, justifying, or misrepresenting the residential school system.
what_it_does: Creates a new offence for statements, other than in private conversation, that wilfully promote hatred against Indigenous peoples by condoning, denying, downplaying, justifying, or misrepresenting the Indian residential school system.
Sets the penalty for that offence at up to 2 years in prison if prosecuted by indictment, or a lesser penalty on summary conviction.

Provides defences if the statements are true, are made in good faith on a religious subject, are part of public-interest discussion believed true on reasonable grounds, or are made in good faith to remove hateful material.
Applies the existing rules on forfeiture, seizure of communication facilities, and Attorney General consent to this offence, and defines Indigenous peoples by reference to the Constitution Act, 1982.
summary.background: The bill amends section 319 of the Criminal Code. It also contains a coordinating change that would apply if Bill C-9 receives royal assent.
